paragraphs: One of the skills of advanced vibe-wanking is futuristic thinking.
An LLM can teach you a lot if you talk to it about basically any technology.
But the trouble is that it teaches only what the market ALREADY KNOWS HOW TO DO.

Mostly we don't need anything else. For example, everything related to Caddy was invented by the market, and every use case has been polished the fuck out to a state where there's not much left to invent. GPT can explain all of it and help you take possession of that knowledge in half an hour, where before it would most likely have taken weeks.
However, any AI, and all these Codex and Claude APP tools, are things that can do something new. There are no “market playbooks” for them, and they don't really take part in the models' training.
The model can figure out anything together with you. You ask it to take a look at what's new in Codex features, and Codex climbs through the gate to knowledge and comes back with a satisfied smile.
About Caddy it already knew. About itself it has to look.
Accordingly, when we ask Codex to build us some process, it builds a gorgeous one, but at times an already morally obsolete one.
That's where a vibe-wanker needs futuristic thinking. What I mean is easiest to explain with an example:
Take a task: unique copywriting for a warm-up service.

If we want to warm 1,000 mailboxes, that means we'll be sending 20–30 thousand emails a day to Google and Outlook workspace accounts, which will let our mailboxes acquire reputation in their ecosystems.

Obviously neither Google nor Outlook wants “WARM-UP” to exist at all. All their algorithms were created to serve people and to fuck spammers in the mouth, who of course try to automate everything in the world, otherwise their work doesn't make much sense.
The ideal warm-up is:

1) Unique emails
2) Around a given topic (Google catches it if the conversation was en masse about school education and suddenly became about wild high tech).
3) Without any spam triggers like $, SALE, WIN, PARTNERSHIP, STAKEHOLDER in the first cold email
4) With a ragged sending rhythm (a human isn't capable of sending 30 emails strictly once every 15 minutes).
5) Accounting for a human schedule in their time zone (a human isn't capable of working 24/7 seven days a week unless they're a dumbass like me, and those Google is happy to feed into the meat grinder — no loss).
6) With a digestible reply rate (meaning the mailboxes we warm against must also reply back)
7) With ragged conversation depth (meaning the mailboxes shouldn't just reply, we should reply to them too, and sometimes this correspondence may drag on, and sometimes a meeting gets agreed quickly and the thread is concluded).
I won't list every detail — it takes long, you got the idea. There are more than 50 points. Counting the truly micro ones — hundreds.

In the end, if you give the model the task of building the piece of the system responsible for copy quality (what's allowed, what's required, what's forbidden, what's random) — it will by no means do it correctly.
It:
1) Wants to save resources, money, processor time, server capacity, etc. Wants to not because it knows why, but because that's its basic instinct.
2) Sincerely believes that AI is NOT an exact science, and consequently that anything Fully AI can't be trusted. That's also its basic instinct.

So it will try to build an entirely “NON-AI” system, in which, even if we asked for “AI to be in there,” it'll be stuck on like a sleeve sewn to a cunt, and technically won't perform any useful function. It'll just be there for show. The whole semantic load will fall on a multi-level system of little dictionaries and validators of form and content, which in the absence of intelligence will of course work like a piece of shit.

And they will work, mind you. I think some Herman Gref would even give the pot-bellied CTO an award for building such a system out of nothing, by his genius alone. Like Jesus, only instead of water he turned a fucking piece of shit, and not into wine but into diarrhea.

A couple of days later you'll ask, well, how's our warm-up copy, is it working? The system will proudly report after a deep investigation: no, it isn't working! But don't worry, it's designed that way! What else can I do for you?
Suppose at that moment you get smarter and say, like, fuck no, okay, build me a straight-up FULL AI piece, fuck your dim-witted scripted dictionaries.

It'll build it, no problem. Only you don't cancel the instinct with a request like that. It'll build not only an AI-prompted little model that will actually produce real texts, but also a system of ordinary scripted validators with the same dictionaries, which will MANAGE THE PROCESS.
That is, it won't be AI managing scripts, it'll be scripts managing AI.
That's exactly how AI thinks right now, because that's exactly how the Internet worked for the last 30 years, and what the model was virtuosically taught in training.

In the end, if the result truly matters to you, you'll rock on this swing until you kill all the scripted validators. The model will resist strongly, but it'll obey if prompted correctly, and you'll be left with a naked AI process, with a prompt at the input and whatever that prompt does at the output.
And managing the quality of the result is no longer a scripting task but a task of finding balance between:

1) Model type (the price tag per unit of its creation)
2) Model settings (temperature etc.)
3) Whether you need two or three or four or ten layers of models so that one checks and improves the output of the previous one down the chain
4) The prompt
5) The project structure — what the model has access to at all and which endpoints are available to it as a result of the work done

The more precise the models get, the less code is needed. I've arrived at a point where some VERY IMPORTANT areas of my project consist entirely of front end alone, in code terms. On the back end there are exclusively neural nets, and debugging is exclusively debugging cost against quality.

Many processes that work significantly better on deep reasoning and don't need an instant reaction to a button press on the front end are most profitable of all to wire in through a launched Codex session in headless mode with access TO THE WHOLE SERVER and a damn meticulously polished prompt.

Frankly, I only very recently arrived at this. For several months I tried to generate some fucked-up code constructs that worked, but without AI reasoning their weakness is that the task needs someone's reasoning in order to execute. And if it's not AI, then it's a human.

Very few functions (and as a rule they're very dumb functions) can be implemented reliably by scripting methods. That's actually why SaaS is so fucking awful. People are forced to use it, but nobody loves it.

Because SaaS gives a heap of buttons, but people have to press those buttons. SaaS can't think through a scheme without reasoning here and there so that the automation itself makes the whole needed scope of decisions. So we take a human, give him 1,000 buttons, and watch him dance across them with tears in his eyes.

You don't have to do that anymore. A product manager should sit and decide where and how many digital models should think so that the output is guaranteed good. That's what they'll pay for in the coming year. If, of course, the market even manages to mature enough to form a need for such product managers, before AI first gets smart enough to start deciding for people what to do and how.
And based on the above, I don't just believe but see with my own eyes how the Internet will very soon become Codeless.
Code simply isn't needed. The Internet will become alive, like a Zerg ship. Little fuckers will jump out of it and fuck all the Terrans up the ass.
The benefit of the masses' on-average templated thinking is that it's easier to find common grounds with those masses.
With some writer, engineer and especially artist — fuck knows what's on their mind. You need a remarkable skill set to interest these guys and hold onto that interest long enough.

Whereas a simple Joe, who's satisfied with 5 categories of action per day, switches on his tower at school and before death. You tell him some simple thought, preferably one that also criticizes someone, because then Joe not only participates in the global news field but is also not part of the censured group (otherwise he'd have kept the news quiet), and thanks to that he sort of ascends straight to the heavens inside himself.
AI is now at such an early stage of penetration into the masses that any essentially mass knowledge is exclusively the echo of a horde of people who don't know what they're talking about at all.

This happens because people who don't understand the subject will easily believe any embellishment, a.k.a. bullshit, and bullshit at this stage of a market usually differs from reality very, very strongly, sometimes by 100 and by 10,000 times. Accordingly, only bullshit gets pushed, since the truth looks too insignificant against its backdrop to shout about, and in the general conversational background a smart person has absolutely nothing to do — he's one-on-one with the technology and should trust only himself.

Yesterday I once again talked with a guy who's at the stage where he boasts of being up to his ears in vibe-coding by telling how last week he installed OpenClaw on a Mac mini and connected his Telegram to it =)))))))))))))))))
And now of course he needs no fewer than fifteen monitors so this OpenClaw displays reliably enough in Telegram)))))

Fucking shameful… Into the same category goes the girl who the day before yesterday was telling me that without the Get Shit Done skill set it's impossible to use coding agents so that they do anything at all.
And of course every month the muttering about the most gigantic inflated AI bubble spreads in waves across the lake of public opinion…

“ANTHROPIC IPO VALUATION: $950B
SAMSUNG VALUATION: $850B

ANTHROPIC REVENUE: $20B
SAMSUNG REVENUE: $230B
The AI Bubble is running exact same 1999 script.”
Everyone's pushing this shit and going ha ha ha, fuck, how DUMB the billionaires in the States are, if only Zadornov could snort along now..
But the truth is that Anthropic and OpenAI are most likely, at this stage, still fucking hugely Undervalued companies.

Despite the fact that I've known Samsung and its devices as long as I've lived, and Anthropic and OpenAI for fuck all, if the company Samsung ceased to exist tomorrow — I wouldn't notice. If OpenAI ceased to exist, I'd be fucking floored uncontrollably.
Or you can look at it from this angle: all the powers that be have already stated how AI will multiply the economy by at least 10 by 2040.
And the economy is, like, 200-and-fucking-something trillion, on paper at least.
So how much should a company like Anthropic be worth then? =)))

By the way, yes, I'm still sitting 14 hours a day, and I've noticed I've reached a level where at parties, when I hear exactly how a person talks about their vibe-coding, I can tell from literally a few words what level of things they can actually build these days =)
Most people are treading water at a very bottom-feeder level, that's a fact. For their level it's generally correct to claim that vibe-coding doesn't work at all.
I think in the end they purely use agents for one-off executions
Whereas actually writing an automation that will do something by itself — you have to sit a lot longer
Not in the sense of coding for a long time, but in the sense of sitting down and figuring out how to vibe-code

Okay, I'm fucking sick of it, time for me to show my shit and drop this unbearable burden of being from my shoulders. On Sunday or Monday I'll be streaming for fuck knows how many hours to show and tell about the technology I've been building all these months =)

There's still stuff to do, but in the night it dawned on me that there's absolutely always stuff to do, despite the fact that every week I tell myself I'll finish by the end of the week, and at the end, instead of a celebration, I invent two weeks of backlog ahead =)
For a long time now my system has been the best thing on the market, hands down. Simply zero doubt that nobody has anything even close to this shit)
If someone starts showing off and claiming they do — they're a bullshitter, because they won't be able to show it. And I'll show it on stream;)
Today in the chat it was said, like, Tim, are you sure you're coding, or have you just lost your mind and are imagining things?
Meanwhile Tim is literally generating tons of leads for live clients with this system.
Enough fucking baiting already. Although it worked.. The world belongs to the brazen motherfuckers!
I have a superpower thanks to having written my first line of code in September
I absolutely don't give a fuck about complex code, simple code, crooked or fucking straight, its appearance doesn't touch me at all, because in essence I can't tell one from another
It seems to me that rather than refactoring for fuck knows what reason, it's simpler to run a health check like “what's up with the load on our infra — all okay?”
If yes — then everything's wonderful
And if not, then both Codex and Claude Code miraculously learn to refactor beautifully when they have a task like “optimize the load on the little server”
I know this for sure, because I've run into it more than once on Hetzner, especially on the one for $4.99 a month =)

When you set the task — “please make it so we don't waste a fucking thing anything on load, probably something has to be reworked for that, so rewrite the whole thing from scratch if you must — I don't give a fuck, just make it handle 10 times more on 10 times less hardware, and don't mess with my head in the process plz”
That prompt looks kind of fucked up at first glance
But the output will be exactly what I asked for
And I suppose it happens most likely through the refactor, rewire or whatever the fuck that thing is called that's needed to fulfill this wish
Haha, today I too once again wrote off Opus until their next fucking awesome model:))
Well, honestly I wasn't getting my hopes up at all anymore, but for the UO shard I decided to do everything purely on Opus for two days
Result:
Codex has been repairing the damage Claude did to the repo in two days for five hours now
I don't even want to list what Claude fucked up there
Just bottom-of-the-barrel shit
And in places it's of course a fucking genius
But life is a complex thing
It needs to be not just in places
When people tell me Claude has been their main vibe-coding tool for the last few months, by the way, for me that's immediately the most basic indicator of that citizen's vibe-coding level
Like, what does he do with vibe-coding
Fuck all actually useful. Grinding out something useful on Claude — I just can't imagine that level of stamina
And in some things, precisely from the reasoning point of view, Claude is just a fucking moron
In Ultima there are garden plots
You can grow shit on them
Cotton, hay, fucking grapes, etc.
Claude claimed it had done everything — all the crops work
I look — it doesn't fucking work
I say, bro, but it doesn't fucking work
8 times Claude told me it had fixed everything
But in the end there was a moment when…
My entire map, fuck
The entire HUGE MAP
Was planted with fucking crap
But not the garden plot
It seemed to me it was genuinely mocking me
Like, even the ocean was planted
The bank in Britain was planted
The garden plot is fucking empty
Codex was fucking floored when I told it, like, take a look at a little problem there
And fixed it on the first attempt
How the fuck can that be, how can you count on Opus for anything else if it can't do that
It simply can't match a tile with an ID to another type of ID in the DB and apply a migration?!?!
5.2 did that on the first try
They're not succeeding
They just say they're succeeding
That's a big difference)
It's fashionable now to say you vibe-code
And what's it fashionable to vibe-code on? On Claude!
So I vibe-code on Claude
These people don't understand what they're talking about; ask them a few questions and you hear it right away
What skills do you use?
An enthusiastic enumeration begins
Means he doesn't vibe-code
And there's a fucking ton of these jokes now)
